tagline: A drovers' road laid out ten rods wide, paved narrower.
intro: From Route 2 the road heads west across Exeter between farm fields, then into second-growth woods, over five hills between 290 and 560 feet and down through the valleys of the Queen's River headwaters. For its last stretch it turns onto Victory Highway, built in 1927, and runs to Route 3 under arching trees.

The road was laid out in 1703, ten rods or 165 feet wide, so cattle could graze and water on the way to market at Wickford. Sheep, butter, cheese and wool all came down it. The stone walls that still line much of it mark that old width. In most places the pavement takes up less than 30 feet of it.
season: Autumn, when the red maples in the valleys and wetlands turn scarlet.

moments.title: Eastern Gateway picnic area
moments.text: Under white pines near Route 2, old stone fireplaces sit among the picnic tables, a stopping place for beachgoers in the 1930s and 1940s, according to the 2004 stewardship plan.

moments.title: Exeter Hollow
moments.text: Between Exeter Hill and Chestnut Hill the road drops into a nineteenth-century village where the 2004 plan found a restored mill on the Queen's River, a schoolhouse and old foundations.

moments.title: Chestnut Hill
moments.text: Climbing out of the Hollow, the 2004 plan noted a Baptist church, a Grange Hall and an old cemetery in view at the Chestnut Hill settlement.

sources.label: RIDOT, Route 102 / Ten Rod Road / Victory Highway Scenic Roadway Stewardship Plan (2004), pages 1 to 14
